query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of Hf to the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy can improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective oxide layer, thereby reducing the degradation of its mechanical properties at high temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy in the cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Hf
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: Reduced degradation of mechanical properties due to the protective oxide layer
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance and reduced degradation of mechanical properties at high temperatures
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800-1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 5 hours, Loading: Tensile loading
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Hf to be added and the optimal processing conditions to achieve the desired oxide layer formation are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of untreated and Hf-added equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys after high-temperature exposure in air
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Hf-added alloy shows no significant improvement in oxygen resistance and mechanical properties compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
